title: Algebraic Degree of n-th Roots: Non-Perfect-Power Criterion

problemStatement.formal: For m with prime factor p satisfying p | m but p² ∤ m, and n ≥ 2: (minpoly ℚ (m^(1/n))).natDegree = n and Module.finrank ℚ ℚ⟮m^(1/n)⟯ = n
problemStatement.plain: Formalize the degree bound: any n-th root of a non-perfect-power is a degree-n algebraic number. Specifically, if m has a prime factor p with p | m but p² ∤ m (a 'square-free factor'), then m^(1/n) has algebraic degree exactly n over ℚ.
whyMatters: Extends the prime case of NthRootIrrationalOQ01 to composite m with square-free prime factors
Proves [ℚ(m^(1/n)):ℚ] = n, the field extension degree equals n
Provides the degree-n algebraic number characterization for a natural class of non-perfect-powers
Connects Eisenstein criterion to field theory: irreducible X^n-m → minpoly = X^n-m → degree n

isIntegral_nthRoot: m^(1/n) is integral over ℚ

minpoly_nthRoot_natDegree: algebraic degree of m^(1/n) is n (main result)
